subject: sociology
title: Trends Explained
welcome_lead: Marriage down, divorce up, more cohabitation. Apply key thinkers and laws to explain why the family changed.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure on divorce, secularisation and explanations of changing family life.
final_note: Strong AO2 links each trend to a law, a thinker and a number.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Divorce Reform Act 1969 allowed 'irretrievable breakdown' as grounds for divorce. From 1971 divorces soared. Combined with secularisation and women's economic independence, family life looks very different.
Beck and Beck-Gernsheim's individualisation thesis argues people now choose flexible relationships. Cohabitation has risen sharply, while marriage rates are at historic lows.
Charles Murray and the New Right blame welfare and divorce for an 'underclass'. They favour the nuclear family. Feminists reply that the nuclear family hides domestic exploitation of women.
